newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end near lows after Dow sags.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end near lows after Dow sags.

text.p: SPI Futures 2461 -17 US 30yr cl 6.78 +0.12
10yrbond futs 92.295 -0.105 Gold NY 353.65 Lon fix 354.75

Australian shares finished weaker on Thursday, the market weighed down by a Wall Street fall after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan made cautionary comments at his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
The All Ordinaries index closed 18.4 points lower at 2,464.7, just off its intra-day low of 2,464.4.
The March share price index futures contract ended 17 points lower at 2,459, a 5.7 point discount to the underlying index.
"In summary, the market generally followed the Dow lower after some cautionary statements from Greenspan last night," said John Featherby, a dealer at Perth broker Hartley Poynton.

The dealer said the day's highlight was a deal by Newcrest Mining Ltd to sell its 11.9 percent stake in Normandy Mining Ltd to the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group under a two year equity gold swap arrangement.
Featherby said apart from this there were not too many other highlights with many investors using the weaker session as a buying opportunity in anticipation of further market gains.

Miner CRA, due to report its full year results later today, went against the trend in climbing 7.6 cents to A$19.234, as did fellow miner Pasminco which added seven cents to A$2.39 on the back of firmer base metals prices.

Foster's Brewing shares were busy with over 9.4 million shares traded, the bulk in options and dividend related trade prior to market opening. Its shares held their dividend, closing unchanged at A$2.73, after going ex-dividend five cents.
Capricorn Resources leapt 36 percent to finish at 30.5 cents after some encouraging assay results on Wednesday from its Roundtable nickel joint venture in Western Australia.

The flood of results continued with transport, health care and telecommunications group Mayne Nickless adding 11.2 cents to A$7.67 after reporting a 13.8 percent lower first half net profit of A$43.14 million.

Apart from the sale of its Normandy stake, Newscrest also announced that its half year operating earnings fell to A$8.52 million from A$21.74 million and said it expected to report lower earnings for the full year. Newcrest shares ended 1.8 cents weaker at A$4.882.

Optical products group OPSM Protector lost five cents to A$3.05, despite a 13.2 percent higher first half net profit of A$12.59 million. Victorian-based totalisator betting agency Tabcorp dropped six cents to A$6.02 after posting a 17.5 percent higher first half net profit of A$51.21 million.
Gambling machine maker Aristrocrat Leisure lost a cent to A$3.02 after a first half net profit of A$8.27 million.
In other markets, the Australian dollar ebbed back into a narrow range against the U.S. dollar in late afternoon trade after some soft economic data supressed early enthusiasm.

Traders said volumes had been modest and direction was mainly coming from action on other crosses particularly DEM/YEN where heavy Japanese selling of marks was tending to depress European currencies while supporting the yen.
By 5.05 p.m. (0605 GMT) the dollar was at US$0.7756/61 after starting at US$0.7760/65 from US$0.7749/54 late on Wednesday.

Australian bonds yields ended well below their after hours highs helped by short position profit-taking and further signs of moderating wages growth. Dealers said the market was wary of further fall out from Greenspan's comments on Wednesday.
The yield on 10 year T-bonds closed at 7.67 percent, up 0.09 percentage points from Wednesday's close.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade was solid as traders rolled expiring contracts into later months, while futures trade was moderate despite the heavy turnover in the physical market.
